items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Vasic opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we are gathering from today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share their land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Vasic provided Council with moments of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: I wanted to recognize that last Friday was Trans Day of Visibility and also
notes: World Indigenous Languages Day. As a Council, I think we recognize the devastating, systemic reasons behind why these days exist and how much better we all are when we recognize the strengths and contributions of these communities to our society.

items.title: Canada is home to one of the largest Sikh diasporas in the world, we
notes: recognize this significance through Sikh Heritage Month in April each year.
This month is an important opportunity for us to celebrate the many economic, political, social and cultural contributions of Sikhs in our community and across the country.
Later this month, on April 14, our Sikh neighbours will celebrate Vaisakhi.
Communities and families will come together to celebrate faith, heritage and culture with services at the Gurdwara, shared meals, music and dancing.

This month is an opportunity to reaffirm our commitment to equality, inclusivity and generosity, learning from our neighbours about how to live out these important values. Our city is enriched by the presence and contributions of Sikhs. We strive to be a community that fully embraces and celebrates Sikh contributions.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
notes: That the previous meeting minutes be approved.

items.title: Items Removed From the Consent Motion
2023-2026 Strategic Plan – Draft Scan Report
notes: Sandy Little gave a presentation outlining the results of the scan and engagement completed from November 2022-February 2023. Some of the themes that appeared in the scan include climate change, transportation, recreation, housing, and reconciliation.

The key findings from the Engage Waterloo surveys included being walkable and accessible, affordable housing, and public transit and pedestrian infrastructure. These findings were reflected in the Community Engagement Workshops.

Sandy Little detailed the recent and next steps for the Strategic Planning process, including the public skate that occurred on the weekend, and the draft Strategic Plan coming out on May 8th. She then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-02,
notes: John Vos gave a brief presentation outlining the application, including the existing zoning, the proposed development, and the zoning amendment requested. He then responded to questions of Council.
Trevor Hawkins, Partner, MHBC Planning gave a presentation further detailing the proposed application. He then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.
Councillor Freeman having previously declared a pecuniary interest was absent for the taking of the vote.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Hanmer wanted to shout out the Home and Neighbourhood Associations in Ward 1 for the Easter Bunny Hunts they held this past weekend.

Councillor Bodaly mentioned that the Clair Hills Community Association held its first event post-COVID with a free skate at Albert McCormick on Sunday, April 2nd. He is also looking forward to upcoming Easter egg hunts this coming weekend.

Mayor McCabe attended the KW Skating Club’s Ice Show on Saturday April 1st and wanted to give a shout out to volunteers who help run that. As well, she wanted to shout out staff at the WMRC for their hard work changing the ice over from the ice show Saturday, to the Siskins hockey game on Sunday.
Councillor Vasic and Councillor Roe discussed the Elmira Maple Syrup Festival that occurred on April 1st, and how great it was to see the community out at an event.
